Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 2, Verse 22

“As a person discards worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, so the embodied self casts off worn-out bodies and enters others that are new.”

The Gita's most famous image, and its power lies in how casual it makes the transition sound. Clothes are intimate but not identical to us — the comparison quietly relocates where Arjuna thinks he lives.
